title.en: Speed, velocity, acceleration and the equations of motion

text.en: A cyclist speeds up from rest to 6 m/s in 3 seconds. How quickly did the speed change, and how far did she go? The equations of motion answer both.

Distance is the total path length (scalar); displacement is the shortest straight-line distance with direction (vector).
Speed = distance / time; velocity = displacement / time.
Acceleration a = (v - u)/t, where u is initial and v final velocity; unit m/s squared.
The three equations of motion for uniform acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at squared, v squared = u squared + 2as.
For a freely falling body, a = g = 9.8 m/s squared downwards.
In a distance-time graph the slope is the speed; in a velocity-time graph the slope is the acceleration and the area under it is the distance.
Uniform circular motion has constant speed but changing velocity, so it is accelerated.

problem.en: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s squared for 5 s. Find its final velocity and the distance covered.

text.en: s = ut + 1/2 at squared = 0 + 1/2 x 2 x 25.

why.en: Check: average speed 5 m/s x 5 s = 25 m.

prompt.en: State the three equations of motion and when they apply.

commonMisconceptions.en: Using them when acceleration is not constant

points.en: Speed is scalar, velocity is vector.
v = u + at; s = ut + 1/2 at^2; v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
